full_judgment:
4. Mr. Zinnur Ahmed the learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for the appellant submitted that although preliminary decree was passed as early as 1st. March, 1944 and the appeal preferred against the decree was dismissed on 11th December, 1951, but as the parties had been possessing their respective shares amicably necessity of final decree did not arise and as such application for drawing up of final decree became necessary because in the meantime the landlordism crests were acquired by the Government and the revisional settlement operation started. As the suit plots were recorded under different plot numbers and khatian numbers, and some of the defendants died in the meantime, the parties felt the necessity of having the final decree with necessary amendments in the preliminary decree. The learned Advocate also explained that unless the heirs of the contesting defendants are brought on record correct allotment of shares would not be possible. He also explained that unless the suit plots with their present numbers are described in the decree, it will again lead to inevitable disputes involving further litigations. 

 7. We find there is sufficient force in this submission. The learned Judges of the High Court Division omitted to consider this aspect of the case. So far as the other contention is concerned it appears that it did not get proper consideration either from the learned Subordinate Judge or from the learned Judges of the High Court Division. Change of plot numbers cannot be made a ground for amendment of the preliminary decree but it appears that in view of the long period of time elapsing between passing of the preliminary decree and the final decree, and the wholesale acquisition of the rent-receiving interest of the Zaminders and the raiyats becoming tenants under the Government and the suit plots recorded under different numbers and khatians proper allotment of shares to all the parties including the heirs of the deceased defendants may not be conveniently made by the Pleader Commissioner. But it is a matter for the Pleader Commissioner to note the change while surveying the suit land and reconcile the new plot numbers with the old plot numbers. And on the basis of the report the final decree is to be passed.
